label: input token z during the original phase (not at t=1)
explanation: Fires when the input token is z while the original sequence is being read (t < L), carrying 97% of activation mass. Never fires at t=1 (a z there is silent) and essentially never in the delimiter or copy phase, even when z is input or output. Magnitude is largest for z at middle positions (t=3-6) and when it is the first z of the sequence; z at t=0 or t=2 gives weak activations, and repeated z is weaker. Strongest examples occur in sequences beginning with f/c/q. Remaining missed activations are weak (under ~0.15 of max) firings on non-z tokens near the z-typical positions, mostly in f/c/q-initial sequences.

issues: The claim that repeated z's are weaker and the first z is strongest is false. Among z's at t>=3, repeat occurrences (in_first==0) average about 1.84 mass per unit of recall (mass_recall 0.148 / recall 0.080), against about 1.55 for first occurrences (0.727 / 0.468). Precision is the same for both (0.983). Repeats are equal or slightly stronger, and several top examples have the second z as the peak (e.g. 'q f w [z:0.64] o [z:1.00]', 'z q [z:0.19] o n [z:0.96]').
The core predicate holds. On the test split it scores precision 0.943 and F1 0.885. t=1 has 0 activations, the delimiter and copy phases together have mass 0.0007, and t=3..6 carry most of the mass.

There is one systematic false-positive class: z at t=2. It accounts for 4136 of the 5176 false positives, and about 25% of z's at t=2 are silent (precision 0.753). The explanation only says t=2 is weak. Excluding t=2 or gating it on the first token lowers F1 (0.837 or below), so the original predicate is still the best one tested.

About 16.6% of active steps are non-z (recall of in_tok!=z is 0.162) but they hold only 2.8% of the mass. They are spread thinly across tokens (every token fires at a rate of 1% or less), and conditioning on the previous token being z gives precision 0.008, so I treat them as diffuse weak noise. This matches the explanation.
skeptic.revised_label: input token z during the original phase (not at t=1; weak and unreliable at t=0 and t=2; repeated z's fire as strongly as the first)
